title: Maximum Gap
prompt: Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum difference between two successive elements in its sorted form. If the array contains fewer than two elements, return `0`. You must write an algorithm that runs in linear time and uses linear extra space.

examples.explanation: The sorted form is [1,3,6,9], and the maximum gap between successive elements is 3 (either 3-... or 6-3 or 9-6, the max being 3).
When all elements are identical, every gap between successive sorted elements is 0.

hints: Sorting first and scanning for the max adjacent gap is trivially correct but costs O(n log n) — the linear-time requirement rules out comparison sorts.

Use a pigeonhole argument: if you distribute n numbers across buckets sized just under (max-min)/(n-1), the maximum gap can never occur between two numbers in the SAME bucket — it must occur between buckets.

Bucket sort by value range: for each non-empty bucket, only its min and max matter. The answer is the maximum, over all adjacent non-empty buckets, of (this bucket's min - previous non-empty bucket's max).

solution.approach: Use a pigeonhole-based bucket sort. With n numbers spanning [min, max], divide the range into n-1 buckets each of size roughly (max-min)/(n-1); by pigeonhole, at least one bucket must be empty, which guarantees the true maximum gap never occurs between two numbers placed in the same bucket (since a full bucket's span is smaller than the required per-bucket size). For each bucket, only its minimum and maximum values are needed. Scanning through buckets left to right and tracking a running previous-bucket-max, the answer is the largest difference between the current bucket's min and the last non-empty bucket's max. This avoids ever fully sorting the array, achieving O(n) time and O(n) space.
